title: Barbecue Meatballs
summary: Walnut-sized meatballs with oats and a little deer burger, baked in a sweet smoky ketchup sauce.
credit: Family recipe card from the kitchen of Pam, written for Diane
directions: Heat the oven to 350 F.
Mix the meatball ingredients and shape into balls the size of a walnut.
Place them flat in a pan, one layer thick.
Mix the sauce ingredients, doubling the amounts, and dissolve the sugar. Pour over the meatballs.
Cover with aluminum foil and bake 1 hour.

title: Copycat Honey Baked Ham
summary: A slow cooker spiral ham with a crackly, caramelized spiced sugar crust.
credit: Adapted from The Chunky Chef, inspired by Todd Wilbur

items: 8 lb bone-in spiral sliced half ham

ingredients: 3 tbsp water or ham juices from the slow cooker, for the glaze
directions: Trim the ham if needed and place it in a slow cooker. Stir the melted butter and honey together and rub it over the ham, working a little between the slices.
Cover and cook on LOW 4 to 5 hours.
Heat the broiler to HIGH. Line a roasting pan with heavy duty foil and move the ham into it.
Mix the sugar and all the spices. Pat half of it over the top of the ham.
Broil a few minutes, until bubbly and caramelized.
Put the rest of the sugar mix in a small saucepan with 3 tbsp water or ham juices. Stir, boil 1 minute, and remove from the heat.
Brush the glaze over the ham and broil again 1 to 2 minutes. Watch closely so it does not burn.
Rest 5 to 10 minutes. Serve warm or cold.
notes: Oven method: heat the oven to 275 F. Set the ham flat side down in a foil-lined pan, brush on the honey butter, and fold the foil loosely over it. Bake 12 to 15 minutes per pound (about 1 hr 30 min to 1 hr 40 min for 8 lb). Then continue with the broiling steps.
Bourbon mixed with the water or ham juices makes a nice glaze.

title: Roast Beef 'n Cheddar
summary: Homemade onion rolls, a high-heat top round roast, tangy sauce and cheddar cheese sauce. A copycat of the drive-through classic.
credit: Adapted from Brian Lagerstrom (brianlagerstrom.com)
cook: About 3 hr roast plus 2 hr rolls

items: 2 1/2 tbsp melted unsalted butter, not hot
About 1/2 medium potato, cooked and mashed or riced (75 g)
1 egg whisked with a splash of water, for egg wash
1 medium sweet onion (Vidalia), very small dice
1/4 cup water, plus a few spoonfuls more
Poppy seeds and flaky salt, for the rolls

steps: Heat the oven to 550 F, or as high as it goes.
Rub the roast all over with olive oil. Set it on a wire rack over a sheet pan and salt and pepper it very generously.
Roast 15 to 20 minutes to sear the outside. Lower the oven to 275 F. When it cools down to 275 F, put the roast back in and cook about 2 hours.
Check after 90 minutes. You want about 130 F inside.
Rest at least 30 minutes before slicing.

Put the water, yeast, sugar, egg yolk, butter, potato, dough conditioner, flour and salt in a stand mixer with a dough hook. Mix on medium about 8 minutes, until smooth and pulling away from the sides.
Shape into a ball, cover, and let rise about 90 minutes in a warm spot, until doubled.
Divide into 6 pieces (about 100 g each). Press out the air and roll each into a tight ball.
Set on a parchment-lined sheet pan, cover, and proof 45 to 60 minutes, until doubled.
Brush with egg wash. Top with a spoonful of cooled onions, then a pinch of poppy seeds and flaky salt.
Bake at 400 F for 15 to 17 minutes, until golden but still soft.
Cook the onion in a little oil with the salt, sugar and 1/4 cup water over medium heat until the water is gone, 2 to 3 minutes. Keep cooking 4 to 5 minutes until lightly browned.
Add a few spoonfuls of water to loosen the pan. When it cooks off, stir constantly 4 to 5 minutes more, until golden and sticky. Spread on a plate to cool.
Tangy sauce: mix all the ingredients with an immersion blender.

Cheese sauce: toss the cheddar with the cornstarch. Add it to a pan with the evaporated milk. Heat on low, stirring often, about 5 minutes, scraping the bottom. Add a splash more milk if it gets too thick.
Slice a roll and toast it cut side down in a buttered pan.
Slice the beef as thin as you can. Shaved slices give the right texture.
Spread tangy sauce on the bottom bun, add a handful of beef, spoon on cheese sauce and put on the top bun.

notes: Shred your own cheddar. Pre-shredded cheese often melts oddly.
A long, thin slicing knife helps if you do not have a meat slicer.

title: Brined Roast Turkey
summary: A spiced brine, a hot start and a foil-tented finish give a juicy whole turkey.
credit: Family recipe file, original source not recorded
directions: Bring everything in the brine list, except the iced water, to a boil in a stock pot. Stir to dissolve the salt and sugar. Cool to room temperature, then chill until cold.
Early on cooking day, or the night before, combine the brine and iced water in a clean 5-gallon bucket.
Set the turkey in the brine breast side down. Cover and keep it cold for 6 hours, turning it over once halfway through.
Heat the oven to 500 F.
Microwave the apple, onion, cinnamon stick and 1 cup water in a microwave-safe dish on high for 5 minutes.
Take the turkey out of the brine, rinse it inside and out, and throw the brine away. Set it on a rack in a wide, low pan and pat dry.
Put the steeped aromatics, rosemary and sage into the cavity. Tuck the wings back and rub the bird all over with oil.
Roast on the lowest rack at 500 F for 30 minutes.
Cover the breast with a double layer of foil. Insert a probe thermometer in the thickest part of the breast. Lower the oven to 350 F and set the alarm for 161 F.
Roast until it reaches 161 F, about 2 to 2 1/2 hours total.
Rest loosely covered for 15 minutes before carving.

title: Turkey Breast en Cocotte with Pan Gravy
summary: A whole turkey breast cooked low and slow in a covered Dutch oven in its own juices, with an easy gravy from the pot.
credit: Adapted from America's Test Kitchen, as published by The Oregonian (2014)
ingredients: 1 whole bone-in turkey breast (6 to 7 lb), trimmed
6 garlic cloves, lightly crushed and peeled
directions: Move a rack to the lowest position and heat the oven to 250 F.
Pat the turkey dry and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in the Dutch oven over medium-high until just smoking. Brown the turkey on all sides, about 12 minutes. Move it to a plate.
Pour off all but 2 tbsp fat. Cook the onion, carrot and celery over medium heat until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, thyme and bay leaf for about 30 seconds. Turn off the heat.
Put the turkey back in, breast side up, with any juices on the plate.
Press foil over the pot and cover tightly with the lid. Bake until the turkey reads 160 F, about 2 hours.
Move the turkey to a carving board and tent with foil.
Simmer the juices and vegetables over medium-high until almost no liquid is left, about 15 minutes.
Add the flour and stir until browned, 1 to 3 minutes. Slowly whisk in the broth.
Simmer, stirring often, until thick and about 1 1/2 cups, about 10 minutes. Strain and season with salt and pepper.
Set aside 1 lb of boneless turkey for leftovers. Carve the rest and serve with the gravy.
notes: Skip "hotel-style" breasts with the wings and rib cage still attached. If that is all you can find, trim them off first.
Do not buy a breast over 7 lb. It will not fit the pot.
Leftover turkey keeps in the fridge up to 2 days.
equipment: Dutch oven, at least 7 quarts, with lid

title: Big and Bubbly Focaccia
summary: A tall, airy focaccia with a crisp golden crust, made with a hands-off folding method.
credit: Adapted from King Arthur Baking

items: 1 1/4 cups (284 g) warm water, 90 to 110 F
Flaky sea salt, about 1 rounded tsp

directions: Whisk the flour, salt, sugar and yeast in a large bowl. Add the water and 1 1/2 tbsp oil. Stir until no dry patches remain. Cover and rest 15 minutes.
Do a bowl fold: wet your hand, lift one side of the dough, and press it into the center. Work all the way around the bowl (8 to 12 times), then flip the dough over. Cover and rest 15 minutes.
Repeat the bowl fold 3 more times, resting 15 minutes between each. The dough should feel smooth and strong.
Cover and let rise at room temperature (70 to 75 F) for 1 hour, until nearly doubled and puffy.
Spray a 9-inch square pan. Lay a strip of parchment across the middle with the ends hanging over two sides. Spray it, then spread 1 tbsp oil in the pan.
Move the dough into the pan and flip it once so it is coated in oil. Handle it gently. Cover and let rise 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until jiggly and nearly filling the pan.
Heat the oven to 475 F with racks in the upper and lower thirds.
Oil your fingers and press straight down to the bottom of the pan to make dimples about 1 1/2 inches apart.
Drizzle on the other 1 tbsp oil and sprinkle with flaky salt.
Bake on the lower rack 15 to 18 minutes, until brown on top and golden in the dimples. If needed, broil the last 1 to 2 minutes.
Lift the bread out using the parchment tabs and remove the parchment. Turn the oven off, set the bread back on the lower rack, and let it sit 5 to 7 minutes to crisp the sides.
Cool on a wire rack.
notes: Best the day it is made. Wrap leftovers loosely in foil at room temperature and reheat before serving.

title: Cream Biscuits
summary: Three-ingredient biscuits that are light, moist and flaky. If you can stir, you can make them.
credit: Adapted from Chef John (Allrecipes)
ingredients: 2 tbsp melted butter, or as needed
directions: Put an oven rack in the middle and heat the oven to 500 F. Line a baking sheet with foil.
Stir the flour and sugar together. Stir in the cream until almost all the flour is wet. The dough will be sticky.
Turn the dough onto a well-floured counter and press it into a rectangle about 1/2 inch thick. Fold it in thirds, then press it out again.
Roll it to about 6x10 inches and 1/2 inch thick. Cut rounds with a 3-inch cutter. Press the scraps together, roll again, and cut more.
Set the biscuits on the baking sheet and brush the tops with melted butter.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes, until golden brown.
Brush with butter again and let stand 2 to 3 minutes before serving.
notes: No self-rising flour? Stir 1 tbsp baking powder and 1 tsp salt into 2 cups all-purpose flour.

title: Family Buttermilk Biscuits
summary: Plain shortening biscuits from a handwritten family card.
credit: Family recipe card, cook not named
directions: Bake at 425 F on the lower shelf.

title: Dutch Oven Sourdough
summary: A classic round sourdough loaf baked in a hot Dutch oven.
credit: Adapted from Preppy Kitchen (John Kanell)
ingredients: 310 g warm filtered water, 90 F (1 1/3 cups)
500 g bread flour (4 cups plus 2 tbsp)
directions: Whisk the water and starter in a bowl. Add the flour and salt and stir into a shaggy dough. Cover and rest 1 hour.
Stretch and fold: wet your fingers, lift one edge of the dough and stretch it over the middle. Turn the bowl a quarter turn and repeat until you have done 4 folds. Cover and rest 20 minutes.
Do the stretch and fold again. You can do it two more times for a chewier loaf, or go straight to the rise.
Shape the dough into a ball, cover, and let it rise until well puffed, 6 to 12 hours at 68 to 75 F. Poke it with a floured finger. If it mostly springs back, it is ready.
Shape the loaf: lift the dough onto the counter, dust the top with flour and flip it. Pinch the edges into the center, then flip it seam side down and pull it toward you to tighten into a ball.
Set the loaf smooth side down in a floured, towel-lined bowl. Cover and rest 30 minutes. Then chill at least 1 hour while the oven heats.
Put the Dutch oven with its lid into the oven and heat to 500 F for 1 hour.
Flip the loaf onto parchment. Score the top with a sharp knife.
Lift the loaf into the hot pot using the parchment. Cover and bake 20 minutes at 500 F, then lower to 450 F.
Take off the lid and bake about 20 minutes more, until deep golden brown or 195 to 205 F inside.
Cool completely on a wire rack before slicing.
notes: Feed your starter a few hours before you begin. Use it when it has risen and just started to fall.
A cold kitchen means a longer rise. Weighing the ingredients gives the best results.
Score right before baking, and do not press down or the loaf will deflate.
Heating a Dutch oven this hot can discolor enamel. Use a plain cast iron pot if you have one.
equipment: Large bowl, kitchen towel, bowl or colander, Dutch oven with lid, sharp knife or razor

title: White Sandwich Bread
summary: A soft, buttery, slightly sweet loaf for sandwiches and toast.
credit: Adapted from Chef John (Allrecipes)
ingredients: 3 tbsp very soft unsalted butter, plus more for the pan
directions: Pour the warm milk into a stand mixer bowl and sprinkle on the yeast. Wait 10 to 15 minutes, until small bubbles form.

Add 2 3/4 cups flour, the soft butter, egg, sugar, vinegar, salt, baking soda and cayenne. Knead on low until it comes together, adding up to 1/4 cup more flour if needed. Knead on a little higher for about 3 more minutes.
Cover and let rise until doubled, 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Butter a 9x5-inch loaf pan. Scrape the dough in, smooth the top, dust with 1 tbsp flour and press gently. Let rise 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350 F.
Cut a deep slash lengthwise down the loaf. Brush the top with most of the melted butter.
Bake about 30 minutes, until golden brown.
Brush the hot loaf with the rest of the butter. Cool in the pan 10 minutes, then move to a wire rack for at least 1 hour before slicing.
notes: You can brush the top with milk or egg wash instead of butter before baking.

title: White Sourdough (Two Loaves)
summary: A simple kneaded white sourdough that proves on the counter or overnight in the fridge.
credit: Family recipe file, original author not known
directions: Mix the salt into the flour in a large bowl. Add the water and starter and stir to a rough dough.
Knead on a clean counter for about 10 minutes, until smooth, soft and stretchy. A little stickiness is fine. Do not add extra flour.
Return the dough to the bowl, cover, and let it rest 4 hours at room temperature.
Press the air out of the dough and shape it into a tight round.
Dust a proving basket with flour and place the dough in it seam side up. Cover loosely with a towel and prove 3 to 3 1/2 hours. Or refrigerate overnight for more flavor.
Heat the oven to 445 F (230 C) with a shallow pan on the bottom rack.
Turn the dough out onto a floured baking tray. Cut a slash about 1/4 inch deep across the top.
Pour boiling water into the hot pan for steam. Put the loaf in the oven.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until the crust is deep and the bottom sounds hollow when tapped.
notes: The salt amount is low for this much flour. Check it against your taste the first time.

title: Baked Oatmeal
summary: One-bowl oatmeal baked in a pan, with banana, maple and pecans. Good for meal prep.
credit: Adapted from a recipe by Brittany Mullins
ingredients: 2 ripe bananas, sliced, or 1/2 cup unsweetened applesauce
1 1/2 cups chopped pecans, divided, or other mix-ins
directions: Heat the oven to 375 F. Spray an 8x8-inch baking dish.
Stir the oats, baking powder, cinnamon and salt together in a large bowl.
Add the milk, maple syrup, egg, coconut oil, vanilla and bananas. Stir to combine.
Mix in 1 cup of the pecans.
Pour into the dish and scatter the remaining pecans on top.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes, until golden. Cool a few minutes, then cut into portions.
Drizzle with maple syrup if you like it sweeter.
notes: Any milk works. Honey, brown sugar or agave can replace the maple syrup.
Swap the bananas for 1/2 cup applesauce, pumpkin or mashed sweet potato.
Mix-ins can be nuts, fresh or dried fruit, or chocolate chips.

title: Corn Meal Pancakes
summary: Sour milk and cornmeal pancakes fried on a griddle.
credit: Family cookbook page 5, book not named
directions: Mix all the ingredients together.
Fry on a lightly greased griddle.

title: Corn Meal Waffles
summary: Light cornmeal waffles with beaten egg whites folded in.
credit: Family cookbook page 5, book not named
directions: Sift the dry ingredients together.
Beat the egg yolks well and add the milk and butter to them.
Combine the two mixtures.
Fold in the stiffly beaten egg whites.
Bake in a hot waffle iron. Serve hot.

title: Pumpkin Muffins
summary: Easy, moist pumpkin muffins made in one bowl.
credit: Adapted from The Kitchn
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) pumpkin purée, not pie filling
directions: Heat the oven to 375 F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners or spray it.
Whisk the pumpkin, sugar, oil, eggs, pumpkin pie spice, baking soda, vanilla and salt in a large bowl until smooth.
Fold in the flour just until no dry spots remain. Divide among the cups, about 1/3 cup each. They will be almost full.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes, turning the pan halfway through, until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 5 minutes in the pan, then move to a rack to cool completely.
notes: Store airtight at room temperature up to 3 days. Wrap individually and freeze up to 2 months.

title: Bojangles-Style Fried Chicken
summary: Buttermilk-soaked chicken thighs in a spiced flour coating, fried until crisp. Great plain or on a sandwich.
credit: Adapted from The Cagle Diaries (Melanie Cagle)
directions: Stir the 2 cups buttermilk, hot sauce and salt together in a large bowl. Add the chicken, cover, and let sit at room temperature 1 hour.
Pour enough peanut oil into a large skillet to come halfway up the chicken. Heat over medium to about 360 F.
Whisk the flour, cayenne, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, salt and pepper in a bowl.
In another bowl, beat the 1 cup buttermilk, the milk and the eggs until smooth.
Coat a thigh in the flour, dip it in the milk mixture, then back in the flour. Repeat with all the thighs.
Fry about 3 minutes, flip, and fry about 3 minutes more. Check that the inside reaches 165 F with a meat thermometer.
Drain on a wire rack or paper towels.
Serve with biscuits and a side, or on a bun as a sandwich.
notes: Thighs give more flavor. For a restaurant-style sandwich, use chicken breast instead.
A cast iron skillet works well. A deep fryer works too.
Thick thighs may need longer than 6 minutes. Trust the thermometer, not the clock.

title: Dooky Chase-Style Fried Chicken
summary: Whole chicken marinated overnight in a seasoned egg mixture, then dredged and deep fried. Simple and very crisp.
credit: Adapted from Chef John (Allrecipes), inspired by the New Orleans restaurant Dooky Chase

items: 1 whole chicken (4 lb), cut into 8 pieces, or 4 lb bone-in, skin-on pieces

directions: Mix the salt, pepper, garlic powder and cayenne in a small bowl.
Whisk the eggs, water and 2 tbsp of the spice mix in a bowl big enough for all the chicken.
Cut the chicken into 2 breast halves, 2 thighs, 2 drumsticks and 2 wings.
Toss the chicken in the egg mix and press it down so it is covered. Cover and refrigerate 12 to 24 hours, tossing it several times.
Stir the flour and 1 tsp salt together in a shallow pan.
Heat the oil to 350 F.
Lift each piece from the marinade and let the extra drip off. Coat in flour and shake off the excess.
Add the breast pieces to the oil first and fry 3 to 4 minutes. Then add the thighs, legs and wings.
Fry 15 to 18 minutes more, until the juices run clear and the center reads at least 165 F.
Drain on a rack and cool 5 minutes before serving.
notes: You can fry after a few hours of marinating, but overnight is best.

title: Corn Bread (Family Cookbook)
summary: A sweet cornbread made with brown sugar, cornmeal and flour. Page 5 of a family cookbook.
credit: Family cookbook page 5, book not named
serves: One 13x7-inch pan or two 8-inch square pans
directions: Heat the oven to 350 F. Grease the pan or pans.
Sift together the dry ingredients.
Add the butter, beaten eggs and milk.
Bake in one greased 13x7-inch cake pan, or two 8-inch square pans, for 25 minutes.

title: Corn Meal Mush
summary: Old-fashioned boiled cornmeal, served with butter, sugar or cream. Leftovers can be fried.
credit: Family cookbook page 5, book not named
ingredients: 3 1/2 cups unsifted cornmeal, or 3 cups sifted
directions: Heat 4 cups water to boiling in a heavy saucepan.
Add the salt to the cornmeal. Add the 2 cups cold water to it.
Stir the cornmeal mixture slowly into the boiling water.
Simmer 1/2 hour.
Serve with butter, sugar or cream, as you like.

title: Fried Cornbread
summary: Crusty outside, soft inside. Silver dollar sized cakes fried in a skillet.
credit: Adapted from Grandbaby Cakes (Jocelyn Delk Adams)
directions: Mix the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, salt and sugar in a large bowl.
Mix the buttermilk and egg together, then stir into the dry ingredients until no dry spots remain. It will look more like dough than batter. Rest it about 10 minutes.
Heat 1/4 cup oil in a 10-inch skillet over medium heat.
Drop in heaping tablespoons of dough, 3 or 4 at a time. Fry 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden.
Drain on paper towels. Add the rest of the oil halfway through.
Serve right away.
notes: The oil should sizzle when the dough hits it, but not smoke. Medium heat is usually right.
Keep the cakes small so they cook evenly and flip easily.
Do not crowd the skillet, or the oil cools down.

title: Fried Mush
summary: Leftover cornmeal mush set in a loaf pan, then sliced and fried.
credit: Family cookbook page 5, book not named
ingredients: 2 tbsp shortening, for each cup of mush
directions: Stir 2 tbsp shortening into each 1 cup of leftover mush.
Pour into a loaf pan.
When cold and hardened, slice and fry brown on both sides.

title: Hoe Cakes
summary: Thin, crispy, lacy cornbread pancakes made from a muffin mix. Quick enough for breakfast.
credit: Adapted from The G and M Kitchen (Pate Giltner)
ingredients: 2 boxes (8.5 oz each) Jiffy corn muffin mix
directions: Stir the muffin mix, egg, buttermilk and water together in a bowl.
Heat a cast iron skillet or 9-inch nonstick pan over medium heat. Melt in a bit of butter.
Pour 1/4 cup batter into the pan. Fry about 2 1/2 minutes, until the batter is almost set.
Flip and fry another 2 1/2 minutes.
Move to a plate and repeat. Serve with butter, jam or maple syrup.
notes: Skip the water if you want thicker, more pancake-like cakes.
Heat should be a little warmer than medium. Too hot burns the butter, too low will not brown the cakes.

title: Wet Cornbread
summary: A sweet, custard-style cornbread from the Eastern Shore. It bakes low and slow and settles as it cools.
credit: Adapted from My Dragonfly Cafe, a grandmother's recipe from the Eastern Shore
directions: Heat the oven to 350 F. Line an 8x8-inch pan with two strips of parchment, or grease it well.
Whisk the cornmeal, sugar and baking powder together.
Beat the eggs into the milk until smooth.
Bring the water and butter to a low boil in a medium saucepan. Simmer just until the butter melts.
Whisk the dry mix into the water. Slowly pour in the milk and eggs, whisking the whole time.
Keep whisking over low heat until it thickens like custard. Pour into the pan and smooth the top.
Bake 90 minutes on the middle rack, until the top is golden. It may look patchy.
Cool on a rack. It will settle over about an hour. Slice when cooled but still warm.

title: Snickerdoodles
summary: Soft, chewy cookies rolled in cinnamon sugar.
credit: Source site not recorded in the file
directions: Heat the oven to 400 F. Line two baking sheets with parchment.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt together.
Cream the butter and 1 1/2 cups sugar until light and fluffy, 2 to 3 minutes. Beat in the eggs one at a time.
Add the flour mixture gradually. Mix just until combined.
Stir the 1/2 cup sugar and cinnamon together in a small bowl.
Roll the dough into 1-inch balls and roll each generously in the cinnamon sugar.
Set them 2 inches apart on the baking sheets.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes, until the edges are set but the centers are still soft. Do not overbake.
Cool on the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.

title: Bourbon Brown Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies
summary: Nutty brown butter, a splash of bourbon and lots of chocolate. The dough chills for 24 hours.
credit: Adapted from I Am Baker (Amanda Rettke), iambaker.net
ingredients: 1 cup (2 sticks, 227 g) unsalted butter, room temperature
1 1/2 cups (300 g) light brown sugar, lightly packed
1 bag (12 oz, 2 cups) semi-sweet chocolate chips
directions: Line baking sheets with parchment.
Melt the butter in a light-colored skillet over medium-high heat, swirling now and then. It will foam. When brown specks appear on the bottom, stir and scrape constantly so they do not stick.
As soon as the butter turns chestnut brown and smells nutty, pour it into a heat-safe bowl.
Stir the brown sugar into the hot butter. Set aside to cool 15 to 20 minutes.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, salt and baking powder together in a bowl.
Whisk the eggs and bourbon into the cooled butter mixture.
Gradually mix in the flour with a rubber spatula. Fold in most of the chocolate chips.
Scoop 3-tablespoon balls onto the lined sheets, about 1 inch apart. Press the reserved chips on top. Cover and refrigerate 24 hours.
Let the dough sit at room temperature 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 350 F.
Bake 12 to 14 minutes, until golden brown. Start checking at 10 minutes for softer cookies.
Sprinkle salt on the warm cookies. Cool on the sheet 5 minutes, then move to a rack.

title: Brown Butter Apple Shortbread Bars
summary: A brown butter shortbread crust, a spiced apple custard filling and a crumb topping.
credit: Adapted from The Kitchn

items: 1 1/2 sticks unsalted butter, cut into 12 pieces
1 1/4 lb tart apples (Granny Smith, Fuji, Pink Lady or Gala), about 4 small, peeled, cored and sliced 1/8 inch thick

directions: Heat the oven to 350 F.

Cook the butter in a light-colored pan over medium heat, stirring and scraping, 8 to 10 minutes. It will bubble, foam, smell nutty and turn dark brown. Scrape into a bowl and stir in 3/4 tsp salt. Cool slightly.
Line the pan with two sheets of parchment crossed, leaving about 2 inches hanging over each side as a sling.
Whisk the flour, both sugars and the baking powder together. Slowly pour in the browned butter, stirring, until a crumbly dough forms.
Set aside 3/4 cup of the dough for the topping. Press the rest into the pan in an even layer.
Bake about 15 minutes, until lightly golden and dry on top. Cool on a rack while you slice the apples.
Raise the oven to 375 F. Whisk the eggs in the empty bowl. Whisk in both sugars, the flour, cream, apple pie spice and salt.
Add the apples and toss to coat. Spread them over the hot crust and crumble the reserved dough on top.
Bake 55 to 60 minutes, until the topping is golden, the apples are tender and the filling is thick like jam.
Cool completely in the pan, about 2 hours. Lift out with the parchment and cut into 12 or 16 bars.
notes: For thinner, wider bars use a 9x9-inch pan and check after 45 minutes.
You can brown the butter up to 3 days ahead. Chill it and melt it again before using.
Pumpkin pie spice replaces apple pie spice. Or use cinnamon with a little ginger, cardamom, cloves, allspice and nutmeg.
Keeps 3 days airtight, or 3 months frozen between sheets of parchment.

title: Brown Butter Chocolate Chip Bars (8-inch)
summary: A smaller, no-chill batch of chewy bars with crisp edges and dark chocolate chunks.
credit: Adapted from Erin Clarkson (cloudykitchen.com)
ingredients: 150 g unsalted butter, cold is fine
100 g light or dark brown sugar
1/2 tsp vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract
directions: Heat the oven to 350 F (180 C). Grease and line the pan with parchment, leaving extra hanging over the sides as a sling.
Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Keep cooking, swirling and whisking often, 3 to 4 minutes, until it foams and turns golden brown and nutty.
Weigh 110 g of the brown butter into a bowl. Cool 15 to 20 minutes so it does not scramble the egg.
Mix in the brown sugar and granulated sugar. Add the egg and whisk 1 to 2 minutes, until lighter and thicker. Mix in the vanilla.
Add the flour, baking powder and salt. Stir with a spatula until just combined, with a few flour streaks left.
Mix in the chocolate.
Press the dough into the pan and smooth the top. Add a few extra chocolate chunks on top if you like.
Bake 20 to 22 minutes, until golden brown and set, with firm edges. Bake a little longer for crispier edges.
Cool in the pan on a rack. Lift out with the parchment and cut with a sharp knife.
notes: The recipe starts with 150 g butter because some water cooks off. You use 110 g of the browned butter.
Keeps 3 days at room temperature in an airtight container.

title: Brown Butter Chocolate Chip Bars (9x13)
summary: Soft, chewy bars with brown butter, plenty of chocolate and flaky salt, made in one pan.
credit: Adapted from Two Peas and Their Pod
ingredients: 1 cup unsalted butter, cut into tablespoon pieces
1 1/4 cups packed dark brown sugar (light works too)
directions: Heat the oven to 350 F. Grease a 9x13-inch metal pan, or line it with parchment.
Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat, stirring often, until it foams, smells nutty and browns, about 5 minutes. Scrape it into a large bowl and cool 5 minutes.
Stir in the brown sugar and granulated sugar until smooth. Add the eggs and vanilla and stir to combine.
Add the flour, salt, baking soda and baking powder. Stir just until combined.
Stir in the chocolate chunks and chips.
Spread evenly in the pan. Bake 18 to 24 minutes, until set and golden. Do not overbake. The bars keep setting as they cool.
Sprinkle with flaky salt. Cool before cutting into squares.

title: Buckeyes
summary: Creamy peanut butter balls dipped in chocolate, leaving a bit of peanut butter showing.
credit: Adapted from Preppy Kitchen (John Kanell)
directions: Cream the peanut butter, butter and vanilla together.
Add the powdered sugar and mix on low until combined. Scrape down the bowl and mix again.
Roll tablespoon-sized pieces (about 20 g) into balls and set them on a baking sheet. Chill until firm, at least 20 minutes.
Melt the chocolate and coconut oil in a bowl in the microwave at 50 percent power, stirring. Let it cool to room temperature.
Dip each ball in chocolate with a skewer or toothpick, leaving a little peanut butter showing on top.
Chill until the chocolate is firm. Smooth over the toothpick holes with a small knife or spatula if you like.
notes: Keeps up to 2 weeks in the fridge, covered.
Scrape the bowl after adding the sugar or the bottom of the mix stays very soft.
Coconut oil thins the chocolate for dipping. Shortening works too.
Use 1 tbsp less butter for a firmer ball.

title: Buttery Coconut Bars
summary: Crisp brown sugar shortbread crust with a sweet, chewy coconut topping. Inspired by a Filipino coconut cake called bibingka.
credit: Adapted from a recipe by Denise Nyland of Panama City, Florida
directions: Heat the oven to 350 F. Line the pan with parchment, leaving ends hanging over the sides.
Stir the flour, brown sugar and salt together. Stir in 1 cup melted butter. Press into the bottom of the pan.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until light brown. Cool 10 minutes on a rack. Lower the oven to 325 F.
Whisk the eggs, condensed milk, flour, brown sugar, melted butter, vanilla and salt until blended. Stir in 3 cups coconut.
Pour over the crust and sprinkle on the remaining coconut.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until light golden brown.
Cool in the pan on a rack. Lift out with the parchment and cut into bars.

title: Chewy Ginger Molasses Skillet Cookie
summary: A big spice cookie baked in a cast iron skillet, chewy with crisp edges and a simple icing. It is soft in the middle at first and firms up as it cools.
credit: Adapted from Food Network Kitchen
ingredients: 1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, room temperature
1 cup sugar, plus more for sprinkling
directions: Put a rack in the center of the oven and heat to 375 F. Grease the skillet with 1 tbsp of the butter.
Whisk the flour, ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, cloves and salt together.
Beat the rest of the butter with the sugar about 3 minutes, until well combined. Add the molasses and egg and beat about 3 minutes, until light in color. Mix in the flour mixture on low.
Scrape the dough into the skillet, spread it to the edges, smooth the top, and sprinkle with a little sugar.
Bake about 25 minutes, until the sides are lightly browned but the center is still quite soft. Cool on a rack 15 minutes.
Icing: whisk the confectioners' sugar with 1 tbsp milk until thick. Add up to 1 more tbsp, a little at a time, until it is thick enough to spread or pipe.
Drizzle or spread the icing on the cookie. Cut into wedges.
notes: Spoon the flour into the cup and level it off. Scooping straight from the bag packs it and makes dry baked goods.

title: Chocolate Chip Cookie Bars (8x8)
summary: Soft, chewy melted-butter chocolate chip bars with brown sugar and vanilla.
credit: Adapted from Preppy Kitchen (John Kanell)
ingredients: 3/4 cup (170 g) unsalted butter, melted and slightly cooled
1 cup (200 g) packed light brown sugar
directions: Heat the oven to 350 F. Line the pan with parchment.
Whisk the flour, salt, baking soda and cornstarch together.
Whisk the melted butter with both sugars in a large bowl. It will be a thick slurry.
Mix in the eggs and vanilla.
Add the dry mix and stir until almost combined. Stir in all but a handful of the chocolate chips.
Spread the dough in the pan. Press the rest of the chips on top.
Bake about 35 minutes, until the edges are set and golden and a toothpick comes out mostly clean.
Cool in the pan about 1 hour before lifting out and cutting.
notes: Line the pan. Do not try to skip it or just grease it.
For a 9x13 pan, double the recipe.
Add 1 cup walnuts or pecans for crunch, or sprinkle flaky salt on top after baking.
For a gooier, brownie-like texture, underbake a little.

title: Divinity Fudge
summary: Old-fashioned divinity with brown sugar and walnuts. A hot syrup is beaten into egg whites.
credit: Family recipe card, cook not named
directions: Combine the sugars, Karo, hot water and vanilla. Boil until the syrup spins a thread.
Pour the syrup slowly over the stiffly beaten egg whites.
Beat until it turns dull looking.
Then add the walnuts.

title: Eva Potts Sugar Cookies
summary: Old-fashioned rolled sugar cookies made with buttermilk.
credit: Family recipe from Eva Potts

items: 1 more cup flour, and more if needed so the dough can be handled

directions: Fluff the butter and sugar first. Then add the vanilla. Add the eggs one at a time. Then add the buttermilk and salt.
Add 2 cups flour, the baking powder and the baking soda. Mix until combined.
Add 1 more cup flour. You may need more so the dough is easy to handle.
Roll out on a floured surface and cut into circles.
Bake at 400 F for 10 minutes.

title: Fluffo Pie Crust
summary: A simple double pie crust made with shortening, or with cold butter.
credit: Adapted from The Edna Muther Family Cookbook (familycookbookproject.com)
ingredients: 1 cup Fluffo shortening, or 2 sticks cold butter
directions: Mix the flour, salt and shortening with a pastry blender until it breaks into small pieces.
Add the ice water one tablespoon at a time, mixing until blended.
Roll into a ball and divide into two pieces.
Roll out each piece on a floured surface for a double-crust pie.

title: Frosted Sugar Cookie Bars
summary: Thick, chewy sugar cookie bars baked in a sheet pan and topped with pink frosting and sprinkles.
credit: Adapted from Six Sisters' Stuff
directions: Heat the oven to 375 F.
Cream the butter and sugar until fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing after each. Mix in the vanilla.
Beat in the flour, salt and baking soda until well combined.
Press the dough into a sprayed half sheet pan.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes, until just golden. Cool completely.
Beat all the frosting ingredients until light and fluffy.
Spread the frosting over the cooled bars and add sprinkles.
notes: Do not double the recipe in one pan. It will not cook through. Use two pans.

title: Giant Skillet Chocolate Chip Cookie
summary: One huge brown butter chocolate chip cookie baked in a cast iron skillet and cut into wedges.
credit: Adapted from Michelle Lopez, from the cookbook Cook It In Cast Iron
ingredients: 3/4 cup (1 1/2 sticks) unsalted butter, divided into 9 tbsp and 3 tbsp
3/4 cup (5.25 oz) dark brown sugar, tightly packed
directions: Put a rack in the upper middle of the oven and heat to 375 F.

Melt 9 tbsp of the butter in the skillet over medium heat. Cook, stirring constantly, about 5 minutes, until dark golden brown and nutty and the bubbling has calmed. Pour into a large bowl and stir in the other 3 tbsp until melted.

Whisk in the brown sugar, granulated sugar, vanilla and salt until smooth. Whisk in the egg and yolk for about 3 seconds. Let it sit 3 minutes, then whisk 30 seconds. Repeat the rest and whisk two more times, until thick, smooth and shiny.
Whisk the flour and baking soda together, then stir into the butter mixture for about 1 minute, just until combined. Stir in the chocolate chips (and hazelnuts) with no flour pockets left.
Wipe the skillet clean. Press the dough evenly into it.
Bake about 20 minutes, until golden brown with set edges.
Cool in the skillet on a rack 30 minutes. Cut into wedges.

title: Grandma's Bread Pudding
summary: Easy baked custard bread pudding with cinnamon and nutmeg. Good with a scoop of ice cream.
credit: Adapted from Live Well Bake Often (Danielle Rye)
ingredients: 1 loaf day-old challah bread (about 20 oz), cut into 1-inch cubes
directions: Spray the baking dish. Spread the bread cubes in an even layer.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, milk, vanilla, nutmeg and cinnamon in a very large bowl until fully combined.
Pour it evenly over the bread so all the bread is coated. Let it soak about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 350 F.
Bake 45 to 50 minutes, until the top is set.
Cool slightly before serving.
notes: French bread or brioche also work. Fresh bread can be cubed and dried in a 350 F oven for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often.
Any milk works, from whole to skim to almond.
Refrigerate covered up to 4 days. Freeze sliced and wrapped up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge and microwave 20 to 30 seconds.

title: Homemade Marshmallows
summary: Soft, fluffy marshmallows you cut from a pan and dust with powdered sugar.
credit: Adapted from Preppy Kitchen (John Kanell)
ingredients: 2 tbsp vegetable oil, for the pan
1 cup confectioners' sugar, for the pan and the marshmallows
directions: Brush the pan bottom with vegetable oil and dust with confectioners' sugar.
Put 1/2 cup water and the gelatin in the stand mixer bowl. Stir and set aside.

Bring the corn syrup, salt, 1/2 cup water and granulated sugar to a boil in a large saucepan over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Stop stirring, and cook until a candy thermometer reads 240 F.
With the mixer on low, pour the hot syrup into the gelatin. Slowly raise the speed to high. Beat until very thick and it forms a ribbon when the whisk is lifted. Mix in the vanilla.
Scrape into the pan. It is very sticky, so use a spatula or wet fingers to spread it smooth.
Leave uncovered at room temperature at least 4 hours.
Dust a cutting board with confectioners' sugar. Loosen the edges, turn out the marshmallow, and dust the top.
Cut into pieces, dusting the knife between cuts. Dust the cut sides so they do not stick together.
notes: Store between sheets of parchment in a dry container. In a cool room they keep about 1 month.
To help with sticking, line the pan with plastic, brush with oil and dust with sugar.
Add food coloring with the vanilla. For pink marshmallows, dust with crushed freeze-dried strawberries.
equipment: 8x8 or 9-inch square pan, stand mixer, candy thermometer

title: Hummingbird Cake
summary: A moist two-layer cake with banana, pineapple and pecans, and a light cream cheese frosting.
credit: Adapted from Chef John (Allrecipes)

items: 2 packages (8 oz each) cream cheese, softened

directions: Heat the oven to 350 F. Butter two 9-inch round cake pans and dust with flour.
Whisk the sugar, flour, cinnamon, baking soda and salt in a large bowl. Add the oil and eggs and mix with a spatula until just combined.
Add the vanilla, pineapple, bananas and pecans. Mix well. Divide between the pans. Shake each pan and tap it on the counter to settle the batter.
Bake about 35 minutes, until a skewer in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pans 10 minutes, then on a wire rack at least 1 hour.
Frosting: beat the cream cheese, butter and vanilla in a stand mixer with the whisk until smooth. Add the powdered sugar in 3 or 4 additions on low speed. Then whip on high until light and fluffy.

Set one cake on a plate. Spread half the frosting on it, leaving 1/4 to 1/2 inch bare at the edge. Add the second layer and press firmly but gently. Pile the rest of the frosting on top and spread outward.
Chill 1 hour.

For the hummingbird, trace a template and slide it under a silicone mat on a baking sheet. Heat 1/2 cup sugar in a saucepan over medium-low until dissolved, hot and amber. Drip it onto the mat to trace the bird. Let it harden.
Set the cooled hummingbird on the cake and decorate with edible flowers.
notes: Pineapple chunks work in place of crushed. Decorate with extra pecans if you skip the flowers.
You may not need all the frosting.

title: Levain-Style Chocolate Chip Cookies
summary: Extra large, extra thick bakery-style cookies with a gooey middle, chocolate chips and walnuts.
credit: Adapted from I Am Baker (Amanda Rettke), iambaker.net
ingredients: 1 cup (2 sticks, 227 g) unsalted butter, cold, cubed
1 cup (200 g) light brown sugar, packed
directions: Line a baking sheet with parchment.
Beat the cold butter and both sugars in a stand mixer with the paddle on medium speed until light and creamy, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the eggs one at a time, mixing well and scraping the bowl.
Whisk the cake flour, all-purpose flour, cornstarch, baking soda and salt together. Add to the mixer gradually on low speed, just until combined.
Mix in the chocolate chips and walnuts.
Divide into 9 equal portions (about 6 oz each). Shape into rough balls without flattening. Set them on the lined sheet and chill 30 minutes, or up to 24 hours.
Heat the oven to 400 F. Line 3 large baking sheets with parchment.
Place the chilled dough balls about 3 inches apart, about 4 per sheet.
Bake 10 to 11 minutes, until golden around the edges but still slightly underbaked in the middle.
Rest 10 to 15 minutes before eating.

title: Lunch Lady Peanut Butter Bars
summary: No-bake peanut butter graham cracker bars with a chocolate peanut butter topping.
credit: Source site not recorded in the file

items: 2 cups graham cracker crumbs (from a food processor)
2 cups Hershey's Special Dark chocolate chips

directions: Grind the graham crackers to a fine powder in a food processor.
Melt the butter with the 1 1/2 cups peanut butter in the microwave.
Pour it into a large bowl. Add the graham cracker powder, confectioners' sugar and salt. Mix well.
Line a 9x13-inch pan with parchment. Spread the mixture evenly in the pan. Refrigerate 20 minutes.
Melt the chocolate chips with 4 tbsp peanut butter in the microwave, stirring now and then, until smooth.
Spread over the crust. Refrigerate at least 1 hour before cutting. This keeps the chocolate from cracking.

title: New York Cheesecake
summary: A classic creamy cheesecake on a graham cracker crust. It cools slowly in the oven so it does not crack.
credit: Source not recorded in the file
directions: Heat the oven to 350 F. Grease the springform pan.
Mix the graham cracker crumbs and melted butter. Press onto the bottom of the pan.
Beat the cream cheese and sugar until smooth. Mix in the milk. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing just enough to blend.
Mix in the sour cream, vanilla and flour until smooth. Pour over the crust.
Bake 1 hour. Turn off the oven and leave the door closed. Let the cake cool in the oven 5 to 6 hours. This prevents cracking.
Chill in the refrigerator until serving.

title: Old-Fashioned Bread Pudding
summary: A simple cinnamon-vanilla custard bread pudding made with day-old bread and pantry staples. Good warm for breakfast or with ice cream.
credit: Adapted from Allrecipes (submitted by ELLENMARIE)
ingredients: 6 slices day-old bread, torn into small pieces
directions: Heat the oven to 350 F.
Put the bread in the baking dish. Drizzle on the melted butter and scatter the raisins over the top.
Whisk the milk, sugar, eggs, cinnamon and vanilla in a bowl until well combined.
Pour the custard over the bread and press gently with a fork until the bread is evenly moist.
Bake about 45 minutes, until golden, the center is set and the top springs back when pressed.
notes: Brioche or challah works especially well. French bread or another sturdy day-old loaf is also good.
Swap the raisins for dried cranberries, chopped apples, chocolate chips or nuts. Add 1/2 tsp nutmeg or a splash of bourbon or rum extract for more warmth.
For a crowd, double it in a 9x13-inch dish.
Bake a day ahead, cover and refrigerate. Reheat before serving.

title: Peanut Butter Energy Balls
summary: No-bake snack balls with peanut butter, oats, flaxseed and mini chocolate chips.
credit: Adapted from a recipe by Nora Taylor
ingredients: 3 tbsp pure maple syrup or agave
directions: Stir everything together in a medium bowl until well combined.
Chill 30 minutes. This makes rolling easier.
Roll into 1-inch balls. If it is sticky, dampen your hands now and then.
Store in the refrigerator 1 week, or freeze for longer.
notes: Use a mix of flax and chia seeds, or hemp seeds.
Almond butter makes a different flavor. Sunflower seed butter works for nut allergies.

title: Pecan Pie Bars
summary: A buttery shortbread crust topped with a sticky, dark golden pecan pie filling.
credit: Adapted from The Kitchn

items: 8 tbsp (1 stick) unsalted butter, room temperature
1 cup all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
3/4 cup dark or light corn syrup
1/4 cup packed light or dark brown sugar

directions: Heat the oven to 350 F. Spray the pan and line it with two sheets of parchment crossed, hanging about 2 inches over all four sides.
Beat the butter, sugar and salt on medium until creamy, about 2 minutes. Scrape the bowl.
Beat in the flour on the lowest speed until a crumbly dough forms, about 30 seconds.
Press the dough into the pan in an even layer using your hands or a floured flat measuring cup.
Bake 20 to 22 minutes, until golden around the edges. Make the filling in the last few minutes.
Whisk the corn syrup, brown sugar, eggs, flour, vanilla and salt together. Stir in the pecans.
Pour the filling over the hot crust and spread it out.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until the filling is set and dark golden.
Cool completely on a rack, about 1 1/2 hours. Refrigerate at least 1 hour or overnight.
Lift out with the parchment and cut into 12 bars.

title: Pecan Upside Down Cake
summary: A moist cake made from a mix, with a sticky pecan topping that ends up on top when you flip it out.
credit: Adapted from Recipes Fiber
directions: Heat the oven to 350 F. Lightly grease the pan.
Stir the melted butter, brown sugar, corn syrup and salt until smooth. Fold in the pecans.
Spread the pecan mixture evenly over the bottom of the pan.
Beat the cake mix, eggs, oil, water and sour cream until smooth and creamy, about 2 minutes.
Pour the batter over the pecans and spread gently to cover them.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes, until the cake springs back and a skewer in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pan about 10 minutes. Run a knife around the edge.
Set a plate upside down over the pan and flip it so the pecans are on top.
Cool slightly and serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Good with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream.
equipment: 9-inch round cake pan or deep dish pie pan

title: Pie Crust (Teresa Pumphrey)
summary: A double pie crust made with shortening, an egg and a little vinegar.
credit: Family recipe card from the kitchen of Teresa Pumphrey
directions: Stir the flour, salt and sugar together.
Mix the egg and vinegar together.
Put the shortening in the flour mixture, then add the egg mixture.
Add 3 or 4 tbsp water.
Bake an unfilled shell at 375 F for 30 minutes.
Bake a filled pie at 425 F for 30 minutes to 1 hour.
notes: A side note on the card lists: filling, sugar, nutmeg, cinnamon.

title: Pumpkin Snickerdoodle Bars
summary: Chewy pumpkin blondies with a cinnamon sugar top.
credit: Adapted from The Kitchn
ingredients: Cooking spray or butter, for the pan
1/2 cup plus 3 tbsp granulated sugar, divided
1/2 cup packed light or dark brown sugar
1/2 cup pumpkin purée, not pie filling
directions: Heat the oven to 350 F.
Melt the butter in a large microwave-safe bowl, 50 to 60 seconds, or in a small saucepan. Set aside about 5 minutes to cool.
Line the pan with parchment, leaving an overhang on two sides. Coat the pan and parchment with spray or butter.
Whisk 3 tbsp of the granulated sugar with 2 tsp of the pumpkin pie spice in a small bowl.
Add the remaining 1/2 cup granulated sugar, the brown sugar, pumpkin, vanilla and salt to the butter. Stir until smooth and glossy.
Sprinkle the remaining 1/2 tsp pumpkin pie spice, the cream of tartar, baking powder and baking soda over the mixture. Add the flour and stir until a thick batter forms.
Spread the batter in the pan. Sprinkle on the cinnamon sugar and lightly press it in.
Bake 15 minutes. Turn the pan and bake 13 to 15 minutes more, until the edges pull away and are firm and a toothpick comes out with a few crumbs.
Cool completely on a rack, about 2 hours. Lift out with the parchment and cut into 9 squares.
notes: Store airtight at room temperature up to 3 days, or freeze up to 3 months.

title: 6-in-1 Sheet Pan Cookie Bars
summary: One cookie dough split into six flavors and baked side by side in one sheet pan.
credit: Adapted from The BakerMama

items: Snickerdoodle: 2 tbsp sugar and 1/2 tsp cinnamon
White chocolate macadamia: 1/4 cup macadamia nuts and 1/4 cup white chocolate chips
Oatmeal raisin: 1/3 cup rolled oats, 1/4 cup raisins and 1/4 tsp cinnamon
Double chocolate: 2 tbsp cocoa powder and 1/4 cup chocolate chips

directions: Heat the oven to 350 F. Spray the sheet pan.
Beat the butter and both sugars until well combined. Beat in the eggs and vanilla.
On low speed, beat in the flour, baking soda and salt.
Put the add-ins for each flavor in six separate bowls. Add 3/4 cup of dough to each and mix well. Your hands work best for the dry ingredients.
Press each dough into one-sixth of the sheet pan, side by side, until the pan is full.
Garnish each section with extra toppings if you like.
Bake 20 minutes, turning the pan halfway through, until a toothpick comes out clean. Do not overbake if you want them chewy.
Cool at least 10 minutes before cutting into squares.

title: Soft Sugar Cookie Bars
summary: Soft vanilla cookie bars in a 9x13 pan with a simple American buttercream.
credit: Adapted from Erin Clarkson (cloudykitchen.com)

items: 1 tsp vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract
1 tsp vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract
2 tbsp cream or milk, plus more if needed

directions: Heat the oven to 350 F (180 C). Grease and line the pan with parchment, with some hanging over the edge.
Cream the butter and sugar on high speed until light and fluffy. Add the egg and vanilla. Sift the flour, salt and baking soda together and mix in just until combined.
Spread the dough evenly in the pan with an offset spatula. Sprinkle sugar on top if you like.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until lightly golden and the center looks set. The bars will crinkle at the edges and deflate a little.
Cool completely on a rack.

Frosting: whip the butter, vanilla and salt until pale and creamy. Sift in the powdered sugar and mix on medium until combined. Add cream a tablespoon at a time until fluffy and spreadable. Add color if you like. Run the mixer on low 2 to 3 minutes to remove air bubbles.
Lift the cooled bars out with the parchment. Swoop the frosting on with a spoon or offset spatula. Add sprinkles.
Chill just until the frosting sets, then cut with a sharp knife, wiping it between cuts.
notes: Use the frosting right away, or press plastic wrap on the surface so it does not crust.
Keeps up to 5 days airtight, in the fridge or at room temperature.

title: Supersized Super-Soft Chocolate Chip Cookies
summary: Big, ultra-soft brown butter cookies made with a tangzhong starter and chopped semisweet chocolate. The dough rests 24 to 72 hours.
credit: Adapted from King Arthur Baking (Molly Marzalek-Kelly)

items: 2 cups (426 g) light brown sugar, packed
16 tbsp (226 g) unsalted butter, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 1/2 cups plus 1 tbsp (307 g) bread flour
2 large eggs, cold from the fridge
2 cups (340 g) semisweet chocolate, 60 to 65 percent cocoa, chopped coarsely

directions: Stir the brown sugar and salt together in a large bowl.
Brown the butter: melt it in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Cook, swirling, 5 to 7 minutes, until dark golden with brown bits on the bottom and no more sizzling.
Pour the butter over the sugar, scraping out the brown bits. Whisk hard. It will stay lumpy. Set the pan aside to cool a little.
Tangzhong: in the same saucepan, whisk the milk and 3 tbsp bread flour until smooth. Cook over low heat, stirring, 2 to 3 minutes, until thick and paste-like.
Add the tangzhong to the bowl and whisk until mostly smooth. Whisk in the eggs and vanilla until smooth.
Add the remaining bread flour, baking powder and baking soda. Stir until no dry spots remain.
Refrigerate the bowl, uncovered, 10 to 15 minutes. Chop the chocolate into coarse pieces with a serrated knife. Do not chop it too fine.
Fold in the chocolate. Cover and refrigerate 24 to 72 hours.
Let the dough sit at room temperature 10 to 15 minutes. Heat the oven to 350 F with a rack in the center.
Scoop 85 to 90 g portions for large cookies (about 2 1/4 inches wide), or 50 g for smaller ones. Roll into smooth balls.
Place 3 to 4 inches apart on parchment-lined sheets, five to a half sheet pan.
Bake the large cookies 18 to 22 minutes, or the smaller ones 15 to 18 minutes, until the edges are set and browned. Turn the pan halfway through and bake one pan at a time.
Rest on the sheet at least 15 minutes before moving.
notes: Chopped chocolate wafers or bars work best. If using chips, chop them roughly.
Keeps covered up to 5 days. The crisp edges soften but the cookies stay soft. Freeze baked cookies for longer.

title: Toll House Chocolate Chip Pan Bars
summary: The classic Toll House cookie recipe baked in a jelly-roll pan and cut into bars. Easy for a crowd.
credit: Adapted from Nestle Toll House
directions: Heat the oven to 375 F. Grease the pan.
Mix the flour, baking soda and salt in a small bowl.
Beat the butter, both sugars and the vanilla in a large bowl. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each.
Gradually beat in the flour mixture. Stir in the chocolate and nuts. Spread in the pan.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until golden brown. Cool in the pan on a rack. Cut into bars.

title: Ultimate Berry Crumble
summary: A buttery, tender crumble over a mix of berries with a touch of lemon. Serve with ice cream.
credit: Adapted from Chef John (Allrecipes)

items: 1 tsp apple cider vinegar, or as needed

directions: Heat the oven to 375 F.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a large bowl. Grate in the frozen butter, tossing it into the flour as you go.
Stir in the egg yolks and vanilla with a fork. Add 1 tsp vinegar and mix briefly. Finish with your hands, squeezing until clumps form but the mix is mostly dry. Add more vinegar if needed.
Toss the berries with the sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, zest and cayenne until the sugar and cornstarch mostly dissolve.
Press about half the crumble into the bottom of the dish with a flat cup.
Spread the berries on top. Scatter the rest of the crumble over them, squeezing some into clumps.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until the top is browned and the filling bubbles.
Cool about 30 minutes before serving.
notes: You can use self-rising flour and skip the flour, salt and baking powder.
Any berries work, and ripe peaches or other stone fruit are good too. Frozen berries are juicier.
For a pie-like filling use up to 4 tsp cornstarch. For a runnier one use 1 tsp or leave it out.

title: Ice Cream Base
summary: A rich custard base you can flavor any way you like, then churn.
credit: Source not recorded in the file
prep: 20 min plus cooling, chilling and freezing
directions: Simmer the cream, milk, sugar and salt in a small pot about 5 minutes, until the sugar dissolves. Remove from the heat.
Whisk the yolks in a bowl. Whisking constantly, slowly add about a third of the hot cream, then whisk it all back into the pot.
Cook over medium-low heat until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon, about 170 F.
Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl. Cool to room temperature, cover, and chill at least 4 hours or overnight.
Churn in an ice cream machine as directed. Serve right away for soft serve, or freeze until needed.

title: Chicago Deep Dish (Cornmeal Crust)
summary: A buttery cornmeal crust in a cast iron skillet, layered with cheeses, spicy sausage and thick sauce.
credit: Adapted from Chef John (Allrecipes)

items: 2 tsp olive oil, divided, for the bowl and pan
1 lb spicy Italian sausage, casings removed
1 tbsp olive oil, for the top

directions: Sprinkle the yeast over the warm water in a stand mixer bowl and let it dissolve, about 10 minutes.
Add the oil, melted butter, sugar, salt, cornmeal and most of the flour, in that order. Mix with the paddle, adding more flour as needed, until smooth and elastic.
Knead briefly on a floured counter, roll into a ball, and put it in a bowl greased with 1/2 tsp oil. Cover and let rise 1 to 2 hours, until doubled.
While it rises, simmer the pizza sauce over low heat until very thick, 60 to 90 minutes.
Heat the oven to 425 F.
Deflate the dough and stretch it into a round 3 to 4 inches wider than the skillet. Brush the skillet with 1 1/2 tsp oil and press the dough in, up the sides.
Layer in this order: provolone, fresh mozzarella, sausage, shredded mozzarella. Ladle on the sauce and grate the Parmesan over it.
Fold the crust edges in toward the center. Drizzle 1 tbsp oil over the crust and the middle.
Bake in the center of the oven about 35 minutes, until the crust sounds hollow and the top is browned.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
notes: Instant or rapid-rise yeast also works.
The sauce must be very thick, or the pizza will be soggy.
The source uses its own pizza sauce recipe, which is not included in your file. Any thick, well-seasoned sauce works.

title: Chicago Deep Dish (From Scratch)
summary: A flaky butter crust, homemade hot sausage and a thick tomato sauce, baked 45 minutes.
credit: Adapted from Brian Lagerstrom (brianlagerstrom.com)
prep: About 1 hr plus 12 to 24 hr chilling

ingredients.group: Hot Italian sausage (makes enough for 2 pizzas)

items: Olive oil, a very generous amount
12 to 15 slices full-fat mozzarella, medium thick

directions: Dough: dissolve the yeast in the warm water. Pulse the flour, salt and cold butter in a food processor about 15 seconds. With the machine running, stream in the yeast water. Run 45 to 60 seconds, until it forms a mass between dough and pie crust.
Shape into a ball, cover, and rest 30 minutes at room temperature. Then refrigerate 12 to 24 hours.

Sauce: cook the onion and garlic in the butter over medium-high 4 to 5 minutes. Squish the tomatoes by hand to 1/2-inch pieces and stir in the salt, sugar, oregano, basil and chili flakes. Add to the pan, lower the heat to medium, and cook down by 40 to 50 percent, 15 to 20 minutes, until very thick.
Sausage: mix all the sausage ingredients until slightly tacky.
Take the dough out of the fridge 30 to 45 minutes before rolling. It should have grown about 30 percent. Heat the oven to 425 F.
Coat the pan bottom and sides with lots of olive oil.
Roll the dough on a floured counter to a 14-inch round. Lay it in the pan and press up the sides and into the corners, with no air bubbles.
Shingle on the mozzarella, then the provolone. Add half the sausage (8 oz) in quarter-sized pieces. Spoon on half of the sauce and spread it out.
Top with the pepperoni and a generous amount of Parmesan.
Bake 45 minutes.
Move to a wire rack for 10 minutes to keep the crust crisp. Cut, and garnish with more Parmesan.
notes: Sauce and sausage each make enough for 2 pizzas. Freeze the extra.
equipment: 12-inch deep dish pan or cast iron skillet

title: Crispy Cheesy Pan Pizza
summary: A cast iron skillet pizza with a crisp golden edge. The dough rests in the fridge overnight, and the cheese goes under the sauce.
credit: Adapted from King Arthur Baking (Charlotte Rutledge)

items: 1/2 tsp instant or active dry yeast
1 1/2 tbsp (18 g) olive oil, for the pan
1/3 to 1/2 cup tomato sauce or pizza sauce
Grated Parmesan, Asiago or Romano, and fresh herbs, to finish (optional)

directions: Stir the flour, salt, yeast, water and 1 tbsp oil together until no dry flour is left. Cover.

After 5 minutes, do a fold: reach under the dough and stretch the bottom up over the top. Repeat three more times, turning the bowl a quarter turn each time. Repeat the fold at 5 minutes, again at 10 minutes, and once more at 15 minutes (four folds total).
Cover and rest 40 minutes. Then refrigerate at least 12 hours and up to 72 hours.
About 3 hours before serving, pour 1 1/2 tbsp oil in the skillet and spread it up the sides.
Put the dough in the pan and turn it once to coat. Press it out to the edges, dimpling with your fingertips. If it springs back, rest 15 minutes and press again. Repeat if needed.
Cover and let rise 2 hours at room temperature, until soft and jiggly.
30 minutes before baking, set racks at the bottom and near the top, and heat the oven to 450 F.
Sprinkle about three-quarters of the mozzarella over the crust, all the way to the edge. Dollop on the sauce, then sprinkle on the rest of the cheese.

Bake on the bottom rack 18 to 20 minutes, until the cheese bubbles and the bottom and edges are deep golden. If the top is pale, move it to the top rack for 2 to 4 minutes. If the bottom needs more color, leave it down 2 to 4 minutes.
Run a knife around the edge to keep the cheese from sticking. As soon as you can, move the pizza to a rack or board so the crust stays crisp.
Cut into wedges with kitchen shears.
notes: Putting the cheese under the sauce keeps the crust from getting soggy.
equipment: 10 to 11-inch cast iron skillet (or a 10-inch round cake pan or 9-inch square pan)

title: Detroit-Style Pizza
summary: Thick, airy rectangular pizza with brick cheese baked all the way to the edge, and stripes of sauce on top.
credit: Adapted from Brian Lagerstrom (brianlagerstrom.com)

items: 4 tbsp oil, to coat the pans
2 cups brick cheese, grated (or Monterey Jack and mozzarella)
1 stick pepperoni, sliced about 1/16 inch thick

directions: Stir the dough ingredients together in a bowl. Once it comes together, give it 20 to 30 slap and folds with a wet hand, or use a stand mixer with a dough hook.
Cover and rest in a warm spot 30 minutes.
Stretch and fold the dough 5 to 6 more times, turning it each time. Tuck it into a tight ball.
Cover and let rise 2 hours, until doubled, bouncy, and slow to spring back when poked.
Put 2 tbsp oil in each pan and smear it over the bottom and sides.
Turn the dough onto a floured counter, cut in half, and lay one half in each pan. Press gently. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Stretch and press the dough to cover the pan bottoms. Cover and let rise 45 to 60 minutes.

Sauce: blend 75 percent of the crushed tomatoes with the paste, salt, sugar, basil, oregano and chili flakes. Stir in the rest of the tomatoes. Cook the garlic in the oil until golden. Add the tomatoes and simmer about 25 minutes, until thick.
Heat the oven and pizza stone to 500 F.
Spread the cheese over the dough, all the way to the edges. Spoon the sauce in two thick stripes down each pizza. Add pepperoni and Parmesan.
Put the pan on the stone and bake 16 to 18 minutes. Bake one at a time for the crispiest crust.
equipment: Two 8x10-inch pans (or 8x8 or 9x9, but the crust will be less crisp), pizza stone

title: East Coast Bar Pizza
summary: A thin, crisp pizza with cheese baked right to the edge of the pan. Makes four pies.
credit: Adapted from Brian Lagerstrom (brianlagerstrom.com)

items: 1/3 cup plus 1 1/2 tbsp (100 g) tomato paste
Italian sausage, roasted red peppers, pepperoni or other toppings (optional)

directions: Dough: put the ingredients in a stand mixer with the dough hook. Mix on medium 2 to 3 minutes, until a loose ball forms. Mix on high 5 more minutes, until smooth and clearing the bowl.
Divide into 4 pieces (225 g each) and shape into balls. Put each in an oiled container, cover, and rest 30 minutes at room temperature. Then refrigerate 24 hours or more.
Sauce: add all ingredients to the can of crushed tomatoes and blend smooth with an immersion blender.
Sausage: mix everything, working the meat well.
Mix the mozzarella and cheddar. Take the dough out of the fridge and let it come to room temperature, about 90 minutes.
Put a pizza steel or stone in the oven and heat to 550 F.
Roll a ball to about 10 inches on a floured counter. Prick it all over with a fork. Lay it in an oiled 12-inch pan and press it up the sides a little.
Spread on a few spoonfuls of sauce edge to edge. Add a couple of handfuls of the cheese mix and any toppings. Dust with Parmesan and flaky salt.
Bake in the pan on the steel for 6 minutes.
When the cheese is melted, slide the pizza out of the pan onto the steel. Bake 3 to 5 minutes more to crisp the bottom.
equipment: 12-inch pizza pan, pizza steel or stone

title: Grandma Pizza
summary: A crisp-bottomed sheet pan pizza with shingled mozzarella, hand-crushed tomatoes and garlic oil. The dough rests in the fridge overnight.
credit: Adapted from James Delmage and Tara

items: 1 can (28 oz) San Marzano tomatoes, hand crushed and drained
12 to 16 oz sliced mozzarella, enough to cover the pizza
3/4 cup olive oil, divided (3/8 cup for the pan, 1/4 cup with the garlic)

directions: Dough: put the water in a large bowl. Mix the dry ingredients in another bowl, then add them to the water a little at a time to make a rough, dry mass.

Pour the oil over the dough, scrape the bowl, and turn it onto the counter. Knead 5 to 7 minutes. If it is too sticky, set an upside-down bowl over it for 30 minutes, then go back to kneading (at least 5 minutes in all).

Cover with the bowl again and rest 30 to 40 minutes. Pull the dough into a smooth ball, pinch the seam, and set it seam side down in an oiled bowl. Cover tightly and refrigerate at least 12 hours (up to 72).
Take the dough out of the fridge 2 hours before baking, still covered. Pour 3/8 cup olive oil in the sheet pan. Yes, that much.
Put the dough in the pan and press toward the corners. It will fight back. Cover and rest 45 minutes, press again, and repeat until it fills the pan. Cover.
Heat the oven to 450 F with one rack at the lowest level and one at the highest.
Crush the tomatoes by hand, drain them (save the juice), and stir in 1/2 tsp salt. Stir the garlic into 1/4 cup olive oil.
Shingle the mozzarella over the dough from a corner, leaving 1/4 to 1/2 inch bare at the edge.
Spoon on the tomatoes in diagonal lines or dollops, leaving some gaps. Drizzle 3 tbsp of the garlic oil over the top.
Bake on the lowest rack 12 minutes, turning the pan 180 degrees after 6 minutes.
Check the bottom. If it is well browned, move to the top rack for 6 minutes. If not, leave it on the bottom for 6 more.
Sprinkle with oregano and Pecorino and bake 2 minutes more on the top rack.
Broil 30 to 60 seconds if the top needs more color, watching closely. Rest 5 minutes before cutting.
notes: The dough can chill 12 to 72 hours. In a metal bowl, use a bit more oil so it does not stick.
Use lots of oil. It makes the crisp bottom.
The pizza should be very brown and crisp after 12 minutes on the bottom rack. If it is pale, leave it there for another 8 to 10 minutes.
Leftovers keep 3 days. Reheat at 350 F on parchment about 10 minutes.
equipment: 12x16-inch sheet pan (or a half sheet pan)

title: Ledo-Style Pizza
summary: A Maryland-style rectangular pizza with a flaky crust, sweet marinara and a layer of mozzarella.
credit: Adapted from Spicy Salty Sweet (Leah Greenstein)
prep: About 2 hr for the dough, 1 hr for the sauce

items: Olive oil (the source says 1 1/2 to 2 cups, which looks like too much)

directions: Stir the salt into the flour. Mix the warm water with the sugar and yeast until foamy. Pour into the flour, add 1 tsp oil, and knead 7 to 8 minutes, until smooth. A poke should spring back.
Shape into a ball, coat with oil, wrap, and let rise at least 45 minutes in a warm spot.

Sauce: blend the fresh and canned tomatoes. Cook the garlic, pepper flakes and onion in oil until the onion is clear. Add the tomatoes, black pepper, sugar and salt. Simmer on low 45 to 50 minutes until thick. You need about 1 cup. Cool it.
Heat the oven to 450 to 500 F.
Press the air out of the dough and roll it to a rectangle about 18x10 inches. Prick it with a fork.
Spread 1 cup sauce on the dough. Sprinkle on 1 cup mozzarella and any toppings.
Bake about 15 minutes, or 3 to 4 minutes longer for a crunchier crust.

title: Napoletana Pizza Dough
summary: A cold, slow-rising Neapolitan-style dough.
credit: Peter Reinhart
ingredients: 4 1/2 cups (20.25 oz) unbleached high-gluten, bread or all-purpose flour, chilled
1 3/4 cups (14 oz) ice cold water, 40 F
Semolina flour or cornmeal, for dusting

title: New York-Style Pizza
summary: A cold-fermented dough, stretched thin and baked hot on a pizza steel. Makes four 15 to 16-inch pizzas.
credit: Adapted from Sip and Feast (James Delmage)

items: 10 to 12 oz whole milk, low-moisture mozzarella, shredded
9 to 10 oz crushed tomatoes, mixed with 1/2 tsp kosher salt

directions: Put the water in a large bowl. Mix the dry ingredients in another bowl and add them to the water a little at a time. Mix with a wooden spoon to a rough mass.
Pour the oil over the dough and mix it in. Turn it onto a work surface and knead 5 minutes. If it is too sticky, set an upside-down bowl over it for 30 minutes, then knead again.
Cover with the bowl and rest 30 to 40 minutes.
Divide into 4 balls of about 345 g (12 oz). Pull each tightly into a smooth ball and pinch the seam. Set the balls seam side down in an oiled bowl and cover. Refrigerate at least 24 hours.
Take a dough ball out at least 2 hours before shaping. Put the steel on the second-highest rack and heat the oven as high as it goes for 45 minutes.
Dust the peel with semolina and the counter with flour. Drop the ball in flour, flip it, and set it sticky side up on the counter without pressing out the gas.
Press with your fingertips to stretch it out, leaving the rim untouched and the middle thicker. Turn it 2 or 3 times as you go.
Drape it over your knuckles and stretch to a 15 to 16-inch circle. Move it to the peel and make sure it slides. Add more semolina if it sticks.
Spread on the tomatoes and cheese, staying off the rim. Sprinkle on oregano and Pecorino.
Check that the steel is at least 590 F. Launch the pizza, close the door, turn it after 3 minutes, and take it out after 6 to 7 minutes total.
Cut into 8 slices.
notes: Tight dough balls matter most for New York pizza.
With a pizza stone instead of a steel, add 3 to 4 minutes.
The dough balls freeze up to 3 months after the 24-hour chill. Wrap tightly.
Leftover pizza keeps 3 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer. Reheat at 350 F.
For a stand mixer, mix the water and half the dry ingredients on speed 1 with a dough hook. Add the rest slowly, then the oil, and mix 4 minutes. Knead by hand 1 to 2 minutes.
equipment: Pizza steel (best) or stone, wooden peel, metal peel

title: Sheet Pan Sicilian Pizza
summary: A same-day pan pizza with garlic oil and your choice of toppings. Easy for feeding a crowd.
credit: Adapted from Chef Billy Parisi (billyparisi.com)

items: 6 cloves garlic, finely minced, mixed with 1 tbsp olive oil
1/4 lb crisp cooked bacon, cut in 2-inch pieces
1/4 lb raw loose sausage, in chunks
1/2 green pepper, peeled and thinly sliced

directions: Heat the oven to 500 F.
Put all the dough ingredients in a stand mixer with the hook, or on a clean counter. Knead 2 to 3 minutes on low in the mixer, or 5 to 6 minutes by hand.
Cover with a towel and let rise until doubled, about 90 minutes.
Drizzle olive oil on the sheet pan. Press the dough out to cover the pan completely.
Spread the garlic oil over the dough, leaving a 1-inch edge.
Spread on the crushed tomatoes, also leaving the edge.
Layer on the shredded mozzarella, sliced mozzarella, bacon, pepperoni, sausage, tomato, mushrooms, green pepper, Parmesan and basil. Season with salt and pepper.
Bake 12 to 14 minutes, until browned and cooked through.
Slice and serve.
notes: With smaller pans, divide the dough and make 2 pizzas, or freeze the extra dough.
To reheat, bake at 350 F in the pan or on a tray for 5 to 7 minutes. A microwave works but softens the crust.
Store covered in the fridge up to 4 days, or freeze up to 2 months.

title: Eastern Shore Chicken Barbecue Sauce
summary: A thin vinegar and oil basting sauce for grilled chicken.
credit: Family recipe file

title: Middle Georgia Doctor's Sauce (No Honey)
summary: The same thin, tangy sauce with all brown sugar and no honey, made from pantry staples.
credit: Family recipe
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups Sweet Baby Ray's Original barbecue sauce
1/2 to 2/3 cup brown sugar, firmly packed, to taste
1/4 to 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper or a dash of hot sauce, to taste
directions: Whisk the barbecue sauce, mustard, vinegar, brown sugar and water in a small saucepan over medium heat until smooth.
Stir in the Worcestershire, garlic powder, paprika and cayenne. Add the ketchup here if using.
Turn the heat to low and simmer 6 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sugar fully dissolves.
Take off the heat and whisk in the butter until glossy.
Cool a bit before using. Store in a jar in the fridge up to 3 weeks.
notes: Start with 1/2 cup brown sugar and taste. Add up to 2/3 cup for sweeter.
Let the sugar dissolve fully while simmering or the sauce will taste grainy.
Brush on during the last 10 to 15 minutes of cooking so the sugar caramelizes.

title: Middle Georgia Doctor's Sauce
summary: Bottled barbecue sauce doctored with mustard and cider vinegar for a thin, tangy sauce that soaks into the meat.
credit: Family recipe
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups Sweet Baby Ray's Original barbecue sauce
1/8 to 1/4 cup brown sugar, to taste
1/4 to 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper or a dash of hot sauce, to taste
1 tbsp ketchup (optional, for a thicker, sweeter sauce)
directions: Whisk the barbecue sauce, mustard, vinegar, honey and brown sugar in a small saucepan over medium heat until smooth.
Stir in the Worcestershire, garlic powder, paprika and cayenne. Add the ketchup here if using.
Turn the heat to low and simmer 6 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then. The sauce stays thin on purpose.
Take off the heat and whisk in the butter until glossy.
Cool a bit before using. Store in a jar in the fridge up to 3 weeks.
notes: Start with 1/8 cup brown sugar, taste, and add more for a sweeter finish.
Brush on during the last 10 to 15 minutes of cooking so the sugar caramelizes.
Add another tablespoon of vinegar for more tang.
It is thin by design. Good for mopping or injecting.

title: Bisquick Dumplings
summary: Light, fluffy drop dumplings for any simmering soup or stew.
credit: Adapted from a Bisquick dumplings recipe (author listed as Kathleen)
ingredients: 2 tsp minced fresh parsley, thyme or chives (optional)
directions: Stir the Bisquick and milk together in a bowl.
Drop by tablespoonfuls onto simmering soup or stew. Do not stir.
Simmer uncovered 10 minutes.
Cover and simmer 10 minutes more, until firm and cooked through.
Garnish with fresh herbs if you like.
notes: Never stir after the dumplings go in. It breaks them up.
Keep the pot at a simmer. A hard boil dries them out.
There must be enough liquid in the pot for the dumplings to cook.
Try mixing in 1 cup shredded cheddar or some fresh herbs.

title: Homemade Bloomin' Onion
summary: A whole sweet onion cut into a flower, battered in a seasoned buttermilk dredge and deep fried. Served with a creamy coconut and lime dipping sauce.
credit: Adapted from Mei Lin, as published by Vice Munchies (2019)
total: 45 min (plus 2 hr chilling for the sauce)

items: 1/3 cup (20 g) roughly chopped garlic chives
2 large Maui or other sweet onions

directions: Sauce: blend the coconut milk, coconut cream, vinegar, salt, sugar, garlic, chives, lime zest and juice until smooth. Pour into a bowl and whisk in the mayonnaise and sour cream. Cover and refrigerate 2 hours.
Mix the flours, cornstarch, baking powder and salt in a large bowl for the dredge.

Cut each onion. Trim 1/4 inch off the pointy stem end and peel. Set it cut side down. Starting 1/2 inch from the root, cut straight down through to the board. Keep cutting about 1/2 inch apart all the way around. Turn it over and gently separate the outer pieces with your fingers. Remove the inner root from the center.
Soak both onions in the buttermilk 5 to 10 minutes.
Heat 3 inches of canola oil in a large saucepan to 350 F.
Coat one onion completely in the dredge. Let it sit 5 to 10 minutes while the oil heats.
Fry cut side down first, flipping once, until golden all over, 5 to 6 minutes.
Move to a rack set on a baking sheet. Repeat with the other onion. Serve with the sauce.

title: Homemade Rice-A-Roni
summary: Rice and toasted pasta cooked in chicken broth. An easy side that beats the boxed kind.
credit: Adapted from a recipe by Sara Welch
ingredients: 1 cup spaghetti or vermicelli, broken into 1/2-inch pieces
directions: Melt the butter in a large pan over medium heat.
Cook the pasta in the butter until browned, 3 to 5 minutes.
Add the rice and cook 1 minute more.
Add the broth, salt, garlic powder, onion powder and pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Cover, turn the heat to low, and cook about 15 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and stir in the parsley, and the tomatoes if using.

title: Southern Baked Mac and Cheese
summary: A custard-style baked macaroni with four cheeses and a golden top.
credit: Adapted from Brian Lagerstrom (brianlagerstrom.com)
directions: Heat the oven to 375 F.
Cook the macaroni in well-salted boiling water until al dente, with a strong bite. Drain into a large bowl.
Mix all the cheeses in a separate bowl.
Whisk the eggs, sour cream, evaporated milk, salt and pepper together.
Add the custard, melted butter and about 85 to 90 percent of the cheese to the macaroni. Stir gently. It will be very runny.
Pour into a 9x13-inch dish and smooth the top. Cover with the rest of the cheese.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes, until the top is golden and melted.

title: Norma's Famous Vegetable Soup
summary: A big pot of beef vegetable soup with tomato juice. It takes 4 to 6 hours.
credit: Family recipe from Norma

items: 3 or 4 lb chuck roast and a soup bone, or a package of short ribs for flavor
Salt, pepper and sugar, to taste

directions: Cut the roast into bite-size pieces and boil with water, the bones, salt and pepper until the meat is tender.
Add the cut-up fresh vegetables and the tomato juice to the cooked meat. Cook until the vegetables are tender, adding water as needed.
Add the frozen lima beans and cook in the soup until done.
Add the bouillon cubes, celery seed, and salt, pepper and sugar to taste.
Let it sit and cool so the flavors mix.
notes: It takes 4 to 6 hours to get it all together and cooked.
Sugar to taste takes away the tartness of the tomato juice.
